userStories.title: Switch rorca_recall to DB query; add fetchAll param to rorca_get_memories; deprecate rorca_dump
userStories.description:
Three changes to backend/src/mcp/server.ts:

1. **rorca_recall**: Replace `readMemory(workspacePath)` file read with a direct DB query against the `memories` table (same query `rorca_dump` already uses: `SELECT * FROM memories WHERE workspace_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at DESC`). rorca_recall now reads memories from DB, not the filesystem.

2. **rorca_get_memories**: Add an optional `fetchAll: boolean` parameter (default false) to the existing tool schema. When `fetchAll: true`, the DB query omits the LIMIT clause entirely — returning all rows. When `fetchAll: false` (default), the existing `limit` param (default 20, max 100) applies as before. This replaces the need for any separate "dump memories" tool.

3. **rorca_dump**: Remove the tool registration entirely from server.ts and remove it from the ALLOWED_TOOLS / IDEMPOTENT_TOOLS sets. rorca_dump is fully covered by rorca_recall (full workspace context) and rorca_get_memories with fetchAll:true (all memories). Do not create rorca_get_memories_all — the fetchAll parameter on rorca_get_memories is the correct pattern (parameter overloading, not tool sprawl).
acceptanceCriteria: rorca_recall queries the memories DB table — no readMemory() or fs.readFileSync call for MEMORY.md in the recall tool path
rorca_get_memories schema has a new optional fetchAll: z.boolean().optional().default(false) parameter
When fetchAll:true, the DB query has no LIMIT clause — all memories for the workspace are returned
When fetchAll:false (default), limit param (default 20, max 100) applies exactly as before — no behavior change for existing callers
rorca_dump tool is unregistered from the MCP server — removed from server.registerTool calls, ALLOWED_TOOLS set, and IDEMPOTENT_TOOLS set
No rorca_get_memories_all tool is created — the fetchAll boolean on rorca_get_memories is the only addition
npx tsc --noEmit in backend/ passes with no new errors

userStories.title: Add generateMemoryMd() utility that projects DB memories into MEMORY.md format
userStories.description:
Create a new utility function `generateMemoryMd(workspaceId: string): Promise<string>` in `backend/src/lib/memory-projection.ts`. This function queries the `memories` table for the given workspaceId, groups entries by category, sorts by created_at descending within each category, and renders the standard ledger Markdown format. The output MUST begin with the header comment `<!-- Generated by Rorca from memories DB. Do not edit — changes will be overwritten. -->` followed by a blank line. Each entry follows the format: `## YYYY-MM-DD [Category] Title
> Rule: <rule>
> Context: <context>
> Source: <source>
`. Also add a companion function `writeMemoryMd(workspaceId: string, workspacePath: string): Promise<void>` that calls `generateMemoryMd()` and overwrites `<workspacePath>/MEMORY.md`. Both functions must be exported.
acceptanceCriteria: generateMemoryMd() returns a string starting with `<!-- Generated by Rorca from memories DB. Do not edit — changes will be overwritten. -->`
Entries are grouped by category header (e.g. `# Architecture`, `# Bug Fix`) and sorted newest-first within each group
Each entry renders as `## YYYY-MM-DD [Category] Title` followed by `> Rule:`, `> Context:`, `> Source:` lines
writeMemoryMd() atomically overwrites MEMORY.md (write to temp file, then rename) — no partial writes on crash
`npx tsc --noEmit` passes — both functions are fully typed with no `any`

userStories.title: Pre-run MEMORY.md generation in execution-engine before each story
userStories.description: In `backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts`, before each story subprocess is spawned (inside `executeStory()`, after the WAL `story_started` event and before `buildPrompt()`), call `writeMemoryMd(workspaceId, workspacePath)` from the new `memory-projection.ts` utility. This ensures the agent always reads an up-to-date DB-derived MEMORY.md. The workspaceId is available on the config object passed to executeStory. The workspacePath is `config.cwd`. If `writeMemoryMd` throws (e.g. DB unreachable), log the error with a warning but do NOT abort the story — memory projection failure is non-fatal. The call must be awaited.

After the call, MEMORY.md on disk reflects the current state of the memories DB table (verified by checking file mtime > story_started timestamp in a test)
The generated MEMORY.md header comment is present on disk before the agent subprocess starts

userStories.title: proposed_memories.json handler for opencode/codex agents
userStories.description:
For opencode and codex agents (which have no MCP access), implement a two-part change in `execution-engine.ts`:

**Part A — buildPrompt() instruction**: When `config.agent === 'opencode'` or `config.agent === 'codex'`, append this instruction: `## Memory Instructions\nWhen you discover something worth remembering, append a JSON object to the file .rorca/proposed_memories.json in the workspace root. The file is a JSON array. If the file does not exist, create it with []. Each object must have: { "category": "Architecture|Convention|Bug Fix|Decision|Pattern|Gotcha", "title": "short summary", "rule": "the actionable lesson", "context": "why it matters", "source": "<storyId>" }. Do NOT edit MEMORY.md directly — it is read-only and generated automatically.`

**Part B — post-story hook**: After `markStoryPassed()` and before `writeMemoryMd()` (US-006), check if `.rorca/proposed_memories.json` exists at `workspacePath`. If it exists: parse it as JSON array, for each entry POST to `http://localhost:${config.port}/api/memory` with `{ workspaceId, category, title, rule, context, source }`, then delete the file. Wrap the entire block in try/catch — failure is non-fatal. Invalid JSON in the file is logged and the file is deleted regardless.
acceptanceCriteria: buildPrompt() includes proposed_memories.json instruction for opencode and codex agents only
Post-story hook reads .rorca/proposed_memories.json if it exists after markStoryPassed()
Each valid entry is POSTed to POST /api/memory with correct workspaceId, category, title, rule, context, source fields
The file is deleted after processing (even if some entries failed to POST — best-effort)
Invalid JSON in the file logs a warning and deletes the file without crashing the story completion path
`npx tsc --noEmit` passes

userStories.title: Post-story MEMORY.md rebuild after markStoryPassed()
userStories.description: In `execution-engine.ts`, after `markStoryPassed()` returns successfully (and after the proposed_memories.json handler from US-005 runs for opencode/codex), call `writeMemoryMd(workspaceId, workspacePath)` to regenerate MEMORY.md from the DB. This ensures that any memories saved during the story run (via MCP tool or proposed_memories.json) are immediately reflected on disk for any human or tool that reads the file post-run. If `writeMemoryMd` throws, log the warning but do not fail the story — the story has already been marked as passed. The call chain for a passing story must be: `markStoryPassed()` → `[proposed_memories handler if opencode/codex]` → `writeMemoryMd()` → `gitCommitStory()` → `emitWalEvent('story_passed')`. Rebuilding before git commit means the updated MEMORY.md is included in the story's commit.

userStories.title: Integration test: end-to-end memory consolidation flow
userStories.description:
Write a Jest integration test in `backend/src/routes/__tests__/memory-consolidation.test.ts` that validates the full memory consolidation flow. The test must:
1. Insert a test memory row directly into the `memories` table for a test workspaceId
2. Call `generateMemoryMd(workspaceId)` from memory-projection.ts and assert the output contains the inserted memory with correct format
3. Call `writeMemoryMd(workspaceId, tmpDir)` and verify the file on disk matches
4. Simulate the proposed_memories.json flow: write a valid JSON array to `tmpDir/.rorca/proposed_memories.json`, call the POST /api/memory endpoint for each entry, verify rows inserted in DB, verify file cleanup
5. Call `generateMemoryMd` again and verify the newly inserted memories appear in the output
6. Verify the output starts with the header comment `<!-- Generated by Rorca from memories DB. Do not edit — changes will be overwritten. -->`
Use `afterAll` to clean up test rows from the memories table and close the DB pool.
acceptanceCriteria: Test inserts a memory row and verifies generateMemoryMd() output contains it in the correct `## YYYY-MM-DD [Category] Title` format
Test verifies writeMemoryMd() produces a file starting with the read-only header comment
Test simulates proposed_memories.json: writes file, calls POST /api/memory per entry, verifies DB rows, verifies file is deleted
Test verifies that after proposed_memories processing, generateMemoryMd() includes the newly added memories
Test cleans up all inserted rows and temp files in afterAll — no DB pollution between test runs
`cd backend && npx jest memory-consolidation` passes with no errors

=== GLOBAL STANDARDS (L1) ===
principles:
  typescript:
    strict_mode: true
    target: ES2022
    no_any: "Avoid `any` — use `unknown` with type guards or explicit generics"
    async_first: "All DB calls, LLM calls, and I/O are async — always await"

  error_handling:
    pattern: "AppError class hierarchy with immutable HTTP status codes"
    subclasses: [ValidationError 400, AuthError 401, ForbiddenError 403, NotFoundError 404, ConflictError 409, UnprocessableError 422]
    serialization: "{ error: string, code?: string, details?: Record<string, unknown> }"
    rule: "Throw from route handlers; centralized errorHandler middleware catches and serializes"

  database:
    driver: "pg Pool (async, connection pooling)"
    helpers: "query<T>() returns T[], queryOne<T>() returns T|undefined, execute() returns { rowCount }"
    placeholders: "$1, $2, ... (numbered, NOT positional ?)"
    transactions: "transaction<T>(fn) wraps in BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK"
    migrations: "SQL files in pg-migrations/, timestamp prefix YYYYMMDDHHMMSS for new files, tracked in schema_migrations"
    slow_query_logging: "Queries > 500ms logged with sanitized params"

  validation:
    library: zod
    pattern: "Middleware factories — validateBody(schema), validateQuery(schema), validateParams(schema)"
    method: "safeParse (not .parse() which throws)"
    response: "{ error: firstIssueMessage, details: zodError.issues }"

  llm:
    return_type: "ChatResult { text: string, usage: { inputTokens, outputTokens } }"
    rule: "Always use .text accessor — never treat ChatResult as a string"
    providers: "Multi-provider routing via model registry — claude-cli, anthropic, openai-compat, openrouter"

  api_design:
    documentation: "JSDoc @swagger annotations on every route → auto-generated OpenAPI spec"
    pagination: "{ items: T[], total: number, hasMore: boolean, cursor?: string }"
    response_shape: "Success: res.json(data). Error: { error, code, details } via AppError"
    middleware_chain: "validateBody(schema) → authRequired → async handler"
    security_headers: "helmet (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, noSniff, referrerPolicy)"
    caching: "Cache-Control: no-store on all responses, etag: false"

  testing:
    backend: "Jest with ts-jest, serial (maxWorkers: 1), 30s timeout, PG_POOL_SIZE=1"
    frontend: "Vitest with jsdom, globals: true"
    rule: "Always clean up DB pool connections in afterAll()"

  code_style:
    no_over_engineering: "Only make changes that are directly requested or clearly necessary"
    no_premature_abstraction: "Three similar lines > premature helper function"
    minimal_containers: "Don't add docstrings, comments, or type annotations to code you didn't change"
    security_first: "Never commit .env files, API keys, or secrets. Use vault for sensitive values."

=== SPEC BRIEF (L4) ===
Consolidate the split-brain memory architecture into a single source of truth.

PROBLEM: Two independent memory stores exist today — MEMORY.md (filesystem file, written by agent during execution via file-edit tool) and the `memories` Postgres table (written by `rorca_save_memory` MCP tool and POST /api/memory). These drift independently. `rorca_recall` reads the file; `rorca_get_memories` and `rorca_dump` read the DB. Data loss is mathematically certain.

TARGET ARCHITECTURE:
- DB `memories` table = single source of truth (canonical write target)
- MEMORY.md = generated read-only projection (rebuilt from DB pre-run and post-run; never written by agent directly)
- MEMORY.md still exists on disk so "dumb" tools (Cursor, Copilot, raw Claude Code) can passively read ambient context — the "trojan horse" value

CRITICAL TRAP TO AVOID: Do NOT parse MEMORY.md back into the DB. LLM-edited Markdown is not reliably parseable — silent data loss is inevitable if a heading or bullet is malformed.

HOW AGENTS WRITE MEMORIES (two paths by agent type):
1. claude --print: subprocess inherits ~/.claude/ MCP config, so `rorca_save_memory` MCP tool IS available during the run. Instruct agent in buildPrompt() to call rorca_save_memory instead of editing MEMORY.md.
2. opencode / codex: no MCP access. Agent is instructed to write proposed memories as structured JSON to `.rorca/proposed_memories.json`. Post-run, execution-engine reads the JSON file, INSERTs rows into `memories` table, deletes the file.

CHANGES:
1. rorca_recall: switch from readMemory(workspacePath) [file read] to fetchAllMemories(workspaceId) [DB query] — same as rorca_dump already does. rorca_dump becomes redundant and should be removed from mcp/server.ts.
2. Pre-run MEMORY.md generation: in execution-engine.ts, before each story starts, query DB memories table and overwrite workspace MEMORY.md with a generated projection.
3. buildPrompt() instruction update: for claude agent, add explicit instruction "Save new memories using the rorca_save_memory MCP tool — do NOT edit MEMORY.md directly. MEMORY.md is a read-only generated file."
4. proposed_memories.json handler: for opencode/codex agents, buildPrompt() instructs agent to append to `.rorca/proposed_memories.json` (JSON array of {category, title, rule, context} objects). Post-run hook in execution-engine reads the file, inserts rows via POST /api/memory, deletes the file, rebuilds MEMORY.md.
5. Post-run MEMORY.md rebuild: after markStoryPassed(), query DB and regenerate MEMORY.md projection in workspace root.
6. MEMORY.md format: generated file should have a header comment "<!-- Generated by Rorca from memories DB. Do not edit — changes will be overwritten. -->" followed by the standard ledger format (grouped by category, timestamped entries).
